meta.headline: Every leap second on record has been added, never subtracted
meta.seoTitle: Has a leap second ever been taken away?

dek.text: Has a leap second ever been taken away? The IERS record says every one so far has been an addition, not a subtraction.

assertions.text: Every leap second since UTC began in 1972 has been added to civil time; none has ever been taken away: the IERS table of TAI-UTC runs from 10 seconds on 1 January 1972 to 37 seconds on 1 January 2017, each value one second larger than the last, 27 steps in all.

description.text: Every leap second since 1972 has added a second to civil time, and the IERS record shows none has ever been subtracted.

assertions.text: Every leap second since UTC began in 1972 has been added to civil time; none has ever been taken away: the IERS table of TAI-UTC runs from 10 seconds on 1 January 1972 to 37 seconds on 1 January 2017, each value one second larger than the last, 27 steps in all.

sections.name: answer
sections.heading: Every entry in the record is a step up

sentences.text: The IERS table records the gap between atomic and civil time; across every entry in it, that gap has only ever widened.

assertions.text: Every leap second since UTC began in 1972 has been added to civil time; none has ever been taken away: the IERS table of TAI-UTC runs from 10 seconds on 1 January 1972 to 37 seconds on 1 January 2017, each value one second larger than the last, 27 steps in all.

sentences.text: Every step in that record has added a second; none has ever taken one away.
